subject: surgery
title: Empyema Thoracis, Chest Drainage and Lung Abscess

steps.tx: Pus collected in the pleural space, usually after pneumonia, is **empyema thoracis**. Fever persists despite antibiotics and the patient remains septic. Ultrasound or CT confirms the collection and guides drainage position. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Empyema thoracis collects pus in the pleural space after pneumonia and keeps the patient septic.

vis.alt: Pleural effusion and empyema on chest imaging.
vis.caption: Empyema on chest imaging. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Stripping the thick fibrous peel trapping the lung so it can re-expand is **decortication**. It is needed when organised empyema prevents lung expansion after drainage. Thoracoscopic approaches now achieve this in many patients. Understanding this mechanism explains the symptoms, the investigation findings and the logic behind each step of treatment given.
steps.say: Decortication strips the fibrous peel trapping the lung so it can re-expand fully.

steps.tx: A tube placed between the ribs to drain the pleural space is an **intercostal chest drain**. It removes pus, fluid or air and lets the lung expand against the chest wall. Correct positioning within the safe triangle avoids vital structures. This distinction changes management, so it should be settled early rather than after empirical treatment has already begun.
steps.say: An intercostal chest drain removes pus or air through the safe triangle to re-expand lung.

steps.tx: Drainage through a water filled bottle that lets air out but not in is **underwater seal drainage**. Swinging of the fluid column confirms the tube connects to the pleural space. Bubbling shows continuing air leak from the lung. Careful history taking and examination help place this finding in the right clinical context before treatment is planned.
steps.say: Underwater seal drainage lets air escape but not return, and swinging confirms pleural connection.

steps.tx: A pus filled cavity within lung tissue itself is a **lung abscess**. It follows aspiration, especially in patients with poor dentition or reduced consciousness. Prolonged antibiotics cure most, with drainage reserved for failures. Correlating this finding with imaging and laboratory results prevents both delayed treatment and unnecessary intervention in most patients.
steps.say: A lung abscess cavitates lung tissue after aspiration and usually cures with prolonged antibiotics.

steps.tx: Removal of a lung lobe for cancer or destroyed tissue is **lobectomy**. It removes the tumour with its draining nodes while preserving remaining lung. Fitness testing predicts whether the patient tolerates losing the lobe. Early recognition matters because timely treatment gives clearly better outcomes than waiting for complications to develop first.
steps.say: Lobectomy removes a lung lobe with its nodes while preserving the remaining lung.

steps.tx: Cancer surgery aims for complete removal with clear margins, termed **lung cancer resection**. Lobectomy is standard for early lung cancer in fit patients. Smaller wedge removals suit frail patients with small peripheral tumours. Students should connect this fact with the presenting symptoms, since examination questions usually test that clinical link directly.
steps.say: Lung cancer resection removes tumours completely, with lobectomy standard for early disease.

steps.tx: Empyema progresses through exudative, fibrinopurulent and organising stages, a sequence guiding **stage based treatment**. Early fluid drains easily, fibrin needs tube plus enzymes or thoracoscopy, and organised peel needs decortication. Matching treatment to stage avoids unnecessary major surgery. Documenting this finding clearly in the notes guides the next clinician and supports safe, well planned further management.
steps.say: Empyema stages guide treatment from simple drainage to decortication for organised peel.

steps.tx: Persistent fever a week into pneumonia treatment should trigger a search for **parapneumonic complications**. Empyema is the key diagnosis to exclude. Early drainage at this stage prevents the need for decortication later. When this picture is seen in practice, urgent senior review is wise whenever there is any doubt about severity.
steps.say: Persistent fever during pneumonia treatment should trigger a search for empyema needing drainage.
